Savena — Bologna, Italy

🟡 Local-source safety assessment · 6 areas reviewed individually Methodology →

Relatively safer day Relatively safer night

In detail

Residential south-east, outside the walls: post-war housing, the Parco dei Cedri, and very little that draws visitors. The only finding in local and municipal sources is that its foothill edge is covered by the same Comune neighbourhood-watch pact against house burglary as the hills of Santo Stefano and Porto-Saragozza. Quiet rather than empty, and quiet at night too.

Frequently asked questions

Is Savena safe?

Wandroz currently rates Savena in Bologna as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Bologna during the day and relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Bologna at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Bologna publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Savena safe at night?

At night, Savena is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Bologna. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Savena a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Savena's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Bologna) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
